Check the goodness of fit of a composition model

Source: R/fit_check.R
fit_check.Rd

Runs residual and goodness-of-fit diagnostics on a fitted comp_iv() model, with the diagnostic backend chosen from the model class. Returns a fit_check list holding a tidy tibble of test statistics and the raw backend object. With plot = TRUE it also draws the backend's diagnostic plot and prints the report.

Usage

fit_check(object, plot = TRUE, ...)

# S3 method for class 'comp_iv'
fit_check(object, plot = TRUE, ...)

Arguments

object

A comp_iv object.

plot

Logical; if TRUE (default), draw the backend's diagnostic plot(s) and print the report. The tidy results are returned either way. The clmm, mblogit and coxme fits draw nothing.

...

Passed to DHARMa::simulateResiduals() for the DHARMa backend (e.g., n, the number of simulations, or seed); ignored by the other backends. DHARMa simulates under its own seed (123 by default) and then restores the session's random state. The results are therefore the same in a fresh session and after any set.seed(); only the arguments passed here, such as seed or n, change them.

Value

Invisibly, a fit_check object: a list with

tests

a tibble with one row per check and columns check, statistic, df and p.value (NA where a check has none).

raw

the backend object: the DHARMa simulation, the survival::cox.zph() result, a list of the surrogate residuals and the ordinal::nominal_test() table (clm), or the robustness weights (lmrob, rlmer). It is NULL for clmm, mblogit and coxme fits. The diagnostic plot is drawn as a side effect of plot = TRUE and is not returned; plot(x$raw) re-draws it for the DHARMa and cox.zph backends only.

note

an explanatory note, or NULL.

backend

the backend used: "dharma", "coxzph", "ordinal", "robust", "robust_mixed" or "limited".

model_type

the model class.

convergence

the fit's convergence state as comp_iv() stores it: a one-row tibble with converged (TRUE, FALSE, or NA when the backend reports none), singular and n_warnings (the number of backend warnings captured at fit time).

Details

The backend follows the model class:

lm, glm, lmer, glmer

DHARMa simulation-based quantile residuals (KS uniformity, dispersion, and outlier tests).

cox

survival::cox.zph() (proportional-hazards test and Schoenfeld residual plots).

ordinal clm

sure surrogate residuals, drawn by sure's own plot method as a Q-Q plot and a residuals-against-fitted plot, plus ordinal::nominal_test() (a likelihood-ratio test of proportional odds per term; Christensen, ordinal). The surrogate residuals are random draws made under a fixed seed (123) with the session's random state restored, so they repeat from call to call.

robust lmrob / rlmer

the robustness weights of the MM-estimate (Yohai 1987) or of the robust mixed fit (Koller 2016): the share of observations downweighted below 0.5 (half the full weight) and the smallest weight. A Shapiro-Wilk test of the residuals follows.

mixed ordinal clmm, multinomial mblogit, mixed-effects Cox coxme

fit statistics (AIC and log-likelihood) and a note only. No residual diagnostic is run for these classes, nor a proportional-odds test for clmm or a proportional-hazards test for coxme, and nothing is drawn. For coxme the log-likelihood is the penalized one that stats::logLik() returns, with the fit's effective degrees of freedom in the AIC. For an mblogit fit with a random effect, the convergence line shows mclogit's own flag, which can read as converged although the inner iterations warned. The log-likelihood row is NA.

The header of the printed report carries one line on the fit's convergence (Convergence: converged or Convergence: NOT converged) with the number of backend warnings captured at fit time. The line is left out when the backend reports no convergence state (lm, cox and coxme fits). The same state is returned in the convergence element and has no row in tests.

DHARMa, sure (with tinyplot for its plots) and robustlmm are optional (Suggests) and checked at call time.

References

Christensen, R. H. B. ordinal: Regression models for ordinal data. R package. https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=ordinal doi:10.32614/CRAN.package.ordinal

Dunn, P. K., & Smyth, G. K. (1996). Randomized quantile residuals. Journal of Computational and Graphical Statistics, 5(3), 236-244. doi:10.1080/10618600.1996.10474708

Grambsch, P. M., & Therneau, T. M. (1994). Proportional hazards tests and diagnostics based on weighted residuals. Biometrika, 81(3), 515-526. doi:10.1093/biomet/81.3.515

Greenwell, B. M., McCarthy, A. J., Boehmke, B. C., & Liu, D. (2018). Residuals and diagnostics for binary and ordinal regression models: An introduction to the sure package. The R Journal, 10(1). doi:10.32614/RJ-2018-004

Koller, M. (2016). robustlmm: An R package for robust estimation of linear mixed-effects models. Journal of Statistical Software, 75(6), 1-24. doi:10.18637/jss.v075.i06

Liu, D., & Zhang, H. (2018). Residuals and diagnostics for ordinal regression models: A surrogate approach. Journal of the American Statistical Association, 113(522), 845-854. doi:10.1080/01621459.2017.1292915

See also

comp_iv(), the model object this diagnoses.

Examples

cd <- declare_composition(timeuse, c("MVPA", "LPA", "SB", "SPT"),
                          closure = 1440)
m <- comp_iv(cd, outcome = "obesity", model = "glm", family = "binomial")
if (requireNamespace("DHARMa", quietly = TRUE)) {
  fc <- fit_check(m, plot = FALSE)
  fc$tests
}
#> # A tibble: 3 × 4
#>   check         statistic    df p.value
#>   <chr>             <dbl> <dbl>   <dbl>
#> 1 KS uniformity    0.0381    NA   0.777
#> 2 Dispersion       1.01      NA   0.976
#> 3 Outliers         0         NA   1
